raw_graphql_pull_request.body: ## Motivation The DeepSeek V4.1 Torch prefill indexer computes BF16 scores over request-local compressed keys. On H200, unaligned visible lengths such as 28,799 and 57,343 are significantly slower than nearby 64-aligned lengths. Padding the score width to a multiple of 64 improves GEMM alignment while preserving the logical scoring range. ## Modifications - Restore request-row mapping from per-request local token counts when `req_rows` is `None` under CP. - For BF16 device tensors with a visible length of at least 1,024, pad the dequantized index-key tensor to a multiple of 64 once per request and reuse it across query chunks. - Calculate query chunk sizes using the padded width to respect the existing score-tensor memory budget. - Slice scores back to the logical visible length before causal masking and top-k selection, so padded positions cannot enter selection. ## Accuracy Tests Local validation on DeepSeek V4.1 Flash: - 20 CP request-row mapping cases passed. - 12 score-shape and boundary cases using model-style FP4 inputs passed with exact agreement on valid columns. - 8 Prefill integration cases passed with exact raw-index and KV-slot writeback agreement. - 8 synthetic arithmetic/retrieval probes at approximately 32K and 64K context lengths matched the reference outputs. GSM8K, 1,319 examples per run: | Configuration | Accuracy | Request error rate | | --- | ---: | ---: | | Fresh baseline, run 1 | 96.74% | 0% | | Fresh baseline, run 2 | 96.36% | 0% | | Optimized | 96.74% | 0% | The baseline A/A runs show run-to-run variation. These results do not establish bitwise equivalence of complete generated outputs or replace representative long-context quality evaluation. ## Speed Tests and Profiling ### Setup - Model: DeepSeek V4.1 Flash. - Hardware: 8 × NVIDIA H200. - Prefill: TP4 / CP4 / EP4. - Decode: TP4 / DP4 / EP4. - Prefill BCG: disabled. - Decode and router processes held fixed across comparisons. Both baseline and optimized runs include the same CP request-row mapping fix. The measured differences therefore isolate the score-width alignment change. ### End-to-end benchmark Primary workload: all input 65,536, cache hit rate 50%,70%,90%, output 512 tokens. Results are means of three runs with 512 requests each and 10 warmup requests per run. ### Scoring microbenchmark Timings include the scoring epilogue and, for the optimized implementation, padding. | Query rows | Logical score width | Baseline | Optimized | Reduction | | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | | 582 | 28,799 | 4.113 ms | 2.462 ms | 40.1% | | 292 | 57,343 | 4.088 ms | 2.472 ms | 39.5% | | 582 | 28,800, already aligned | 2.443 ms | 2.445 ms | Approximately unchanged | ### Trace before-cp-rank0: before-cp-rank1: before-cp-rank2: before-cp-rank3: cur-cp-rank0: cur-cp-rank1: cur-cp-rank2: cur-cp-rank3: ## Checklist - [x] Format code with pre-commit. - [ ] Add CI-registered regression tests. - [ ] Update documentation, if required. - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results. - [x] Follow the existing code style. --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): :x: [Run #39758846111](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/39758846111) Latest PR Test (Extra): :x: [Run #39758846147](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/39758846147) Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 10): :x: [Run #39758846145](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/39758846145)

files.patch:
@@ -361,7 +361,17 @@ def prefill_requests(
     ratio = inputs.compress_ratio
     indexer = inputs.indexer
     req, pos = inputs.req_rows, inputs.positions
-    assert req is not None, "the torch indexer needs the batch's rows"
+    if req is None:
+        # CP query rows are rank-local and remain grouped by request.
+        assert inputs.rows_per_request is not None
+        repeats = inputs.rows_per_request_device
+        if repeats is None:
+            repeats = async_h2d(
+                inputs.rows_per_request, dtype=torch.int32, device=pos.device
+            )
+        req = torch.repeat_interleave(
+            inputs.req_pool_indices, repeats, output_size=pos.numel()
+        )
     assert inputs.seq_lens_cpu is not None
     # First flattened-K column of each request row, as inputs.k_slots lays them out.
     k_starts = dict(
@@ -386,6 +396,12 @@ def prefill_requests(
         slots = inputs.k_slots[k_starts[r] : k_starts[r] + lc]
         # Dequantize only this request's visible K rows; the table is pool-sized.
         index_k = pool.get_low_ratio_index_k_dequant(inputs.layer_id, slots)
+        # Keep BF16 GEMM output rows aligned for Hopper tensor-core kernels.
+        # Pad K once per request; padded positions never enter selection.
+        if index_k.is_cuda and index_k.dtype == torch.bfloat16 and lc >= 1024:
+            score_width = (lc + 63) // 64 * 64
+            if score_width != lc:
+                index_k = torch.nn.functional.pad(index_k, (0, 0, 0, score_width - lc))
         request = RequestScores(
             lc=lc, k=min(topk, lc), columns=j, tok=tok, lens=lens, slots=slots
         )
@@ -407,11 +423,13 @@ def _score_chunks(
 ) -> Iterator[ChunkScores]:
     lc, j = request.lc, request.columns
     # Chunk rows so the [rows, heads, lc] bf16 scores stay under the budget.
-    rows_per_chunk = max(1, _TORCH_SCORE_BUDGET_BYTES // (q.shape[1] * lc * 2))
+    rows_per_chunk = max(
+        1, _TORCH_SCORE_BUDGET_BYTES // (q.shape[1] * index_k.shape[0] * 2)
+    )
     for start in range(0, request.tok.numel(), rows_per_chunk):
         rows = slice(start, start + rows_per_chunk)
         tok_c, lens_c = request.tok[rows], request.lens[rows]
-        s = indexer.scores(q[tok_c], index_k, weights[tok_c])
+        s = indexer.scores(q[tok_c], index_k, weights[tok_c])[:, :lc]
         s = s.masked_fill(j[None, :] >= lens_c[:, None], -torch.inf)
         yield ChunkScores(rows=rows, tok=tok_c, lens=lens_c, scores=s)
